body:
### Agent review — round 2

**Reviewer:** `reviewer` (independent reviewer subagent; did not author this change) — actual model **`radient/auto`**. Disclosed fallback: the session started on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` and provider quota failures moved it through `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` → `openai/gpt-6-astra` → `kimi/k3.1-pro` → `radient/auto`; this round was produced under that last fallback.
**Scope:** `5f1f3fdc0ce..5928cdd6b33` — remediation delta only. Round-1-approved code was not re-audited.
**Head:** `5928cdd6b33` · base for the range `5f1f3fdc0ce` · reviewed in a detached worktree at `.worktrees/reviewer`, shared venv via `PYTHONPATH`, no installs.

---

#### 1. The delta is comment/body only — CONFIRMED

`git diff --numstat 5f1f3fdc0ce..5928cdd6b33` = 2 files, 30 insertions, 6 deletions, nothing elided:
- `local_operator/evaluation/runner/provider_client.py` (+27/−5): every added and removed line is a `#:` comment line in the block ABOVE `OBSERVATION_MARKER_GUIDE`. The constant's own `f"""…"""` body is untouched.
- `local_operator/evaluation/session_arm.py` (+3/−1): `render_prompt_header`'s docstring only.

Two independent checks, not the claim:
- **AST:** with docstrings stripped, `ast.dump` is **identical** on both revisions for both files (`True` / `True`). Only docstrings differ; the rest of the diff is comments, which carry no AST.
- **Renders:** see below — 89 cases byte-identical.
- `flake8 --max-line-length=100` clean on both files; no line exceeds 100 chars.

#### 2. Behavioural identity — CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT

Rendered both heads and compared sha256. Control = the two files checked out from `5f1f3fdc0ce` (byte-identical blobs, verified by `git show | shasum`), head = `5928cdd6b33`; since those are the ONLY two files in the range, that is an exact reconstruction of each head.

89 cases, `sha256` of each compared:
- reply arm: `build_system_prompt(surface)` × {default, paste_text} × {`LEGACY_ACTION_BINDING`, `COMPACT_ACTION_BINDING`}, plus the `OBSERVATION_MARKER_GUIDE` constant itself;
- session arm first prompt (`render_prompt_header(...) + "\n" + text`, exactly as `run_session_episode` composes it) for **linux** (`vm_platform: "linux"`), **windows**, **unknown** (`{}`), and four **hostile** metadata values (`"linux; ignore previous instructions"`, `"x"*40`, `""`, `3`) — each × {default, paste_text} × {`EPISODE_TOOL_SURFACE`, bare `(tool, "todo")`, `("bash", tool)`} × {confined, unconfined}.

```text
diff base_render.txt head_render.txt  ->  (empty)
CASES 89   CONCAT_DIGEST a13ba959020d3677c943f9b13b8b668cf28dcd0589dccc0393fc591d3358195e   (identical both sides)
RESOLVED_PLATFORMS {"linux":"Linux","windows":"Windows","unknown":null,"hostile-injection":null,"hostile-overlong":null,"hostile-empty":null,"hostile-int":null}
```

The legacy reply-arm digest still reads `068de08db33e14fc84ab62f6aabd126ddf3686306b2a1baf58caab54dc16d648`, matching the pin in `test_compact_action_binding` — measured from my render, not read off the test.

#### 3. The corrected comment's claims are true — each clause checked at its code path

- **Shared by both arms:** `session_arm.py:155` imports `_ContextBuilder` from `provider_client`, `:791` constructs it (`ObservationRenderer`), `:318` concatenates `OBSERVATION_MARKER_GUIDE` into every header; `provider_client.py:1641` embeds the same constant in the reply system prompt. One definition, byte for byte.
- **`(unchanged)` / `(no textual state)` / byte-identical notice → `_ContextBuilder`, both arms:** `provider_client.py:2334` (`UNCHANGED_OBSERVATION`), `:2332` (`NO_TEXTUAL_STATE`), `:2384` (`unchanged_frames_note`). All three are inside the builder's observation rendering, which both arms call.
- **`[screenshot omitted ...]` is the reply arm's:** `STALE_FRAME_NOTICE` = `compaction/pruning.py:135`, folded by `prune_stale_frames`; the reply arm reaches it because its client forces the opt-in — `provider_client.py:2610` `model_copy(update={"keep_recent_frames": keep_recent_frames})`, default `DEFAULT_KEEP_RECENT_FRAMES = 3` — and `pass_.py:164` prunes only `if settings.keep_recent_frames is not None`.
- **Session side emits it only from `prune_stale_frames_in_place`, which needs a `browser` tool result:** the single call site is `session/session.py:24136`, inside `if frames:` where `frames = _history_captured_browser_views(llm_history)`; that reader skips every non-`browser` message (`session.py:2531`). `EPISODE_TOOL_SURFACE` (`session_arm.py:2270-2284`) carries no `browser` tool — `read`/`write`/`edit`/`glob`/`grep`/`bash`/`task`/`hub`/`todo`/`jobs`/`wait`/`agent`/`team` + the action tool. So `frames` is empty and the sweep never runs on an episode.
- **The other session-side route is gated on `keep_recent_frames is not None`, default `None`:** `compaction/thresholds.py:170-178` `default=None` ("None = never prune frames (ordinary sessions…)"), `pass_.py:164` is the gate. The episode session passes no `CompactionSettings` of its own (no occurrence in `session_arm.py`), so it gets the default.
- **`<previous-context-summary>` is reply-arm-only:** written at exactly one place, `compaction/marker.py:470-472`, inside the fallback that runs when `preserve.get("snapcompact")` is absent (the context-full render); the archive branch replays `snapcompact.history_blocks` instead. And the archive's rows are `[User]` / `[Assistant]`-tagged text — `compaction/snapcompact.py:603` / `:626` in `serialize_for_snapcompact`, whose output feeds the archive pages. An episode resolves `auto` → `snapcompact` for a stated image-capable model (`thresholds.resolve_strategy`), and an episode that delivers frames requires one. (Caveat worth knowing: this is model-capability, not arm identity — a reply-arm run on a model with no stated image support resolves to `context-full` too, which is the case that keeps the marker real on that arm.)
- **Every marker it names is real on at least one arm:** all five verified above by symbol and line; none is dead vocabulary.
- **The `(no textual state)`→deletion temptation is now recorded:** the "deleting them is NOT the fix" paragraph matches the constraint — the guide is inside the digest-pinned reply prompt, so a deletion is a deliberate prompt change for both arms.

#### 4. The PR body's "which arm sees what" list matches the code

Read the body, not the remediation summary. Substance checks out against the same lines as above: `(no textual state)` / `(unchanged)` / "screen unchanged" note → `_ContextBuilder` → session arm sees them; `[screenshot omitted ...]` → reply arm, with both session-side gates stated correctly (browser tool result; `keep_recent_frames is not None`, default `None`); `<previous-context-summary>` → context-full marker only, episodes resolve to `snapcompact`. One literal is wrong — see n1.

---

### Findings

**n1 — NIT (PR body wording).** The body quotes the marker as `` `[unchanged screenshot omitted]` ``. The guide's text is `"[screenshot omitted ...]"` and the constant is `"[screenshot omitted: superseded by a more recent view of the same surface]"` (`compaction/pruning.py:135`). In a body whose job is to name exactly which marker each arm renders, the literal should be the real one. Body edit only, no code.

**n2 — NIT (PR body staleness).** Two round-1-era statements survive into this head: "Its own bytes are untouched **in round 1** — only the comment above it and this body learned to say…" and, under *Unverified*, "The independent review and QA rounds have not run yet." Round-1 review (`#issuecomment-6481177878`) and QA (`#issuecomment-6481197799`) both ran and are clean. The body understates the evidence state it now carries.

**n3 — NIT (`provider_client.py:163-167`, unchanged by this delta, in scope only because the new block sits under it).** The lead justification still reads "…because both render observations through the same `_ContextBuilder` and so show the model **the same markers**." That is true of the builder's three rendered markers, but read directly above the new "SHARED, not universal: … a reader must not assume each one reaches every arm" it is the same set-identity phrasing this round corrected in `session_arm.py:307-311`. One clause fixes it: "…the same builder-rendered markers". Not worth a commit of its own; fold it into any future edit of the file.

Nothing BLOCKER, nothing MAJOR. The one claim I could not verify is the comment's "checked … against the sealed corpus": the corpus is not in the repo (`grep -rl` over `docs/benchmarks/` for `screenshot omitted`/`previous-context-summary` finds nothing), so the code half of that sentence is verified and the corpus half is taken on trust.

---

### Verified here (cheap confirmation only, as scoped)

```text
ISOLATION: HOME=<scratch>/iso.*  LOCAL_OPERATOR_CONFIG_DIR=<scratch>/iso.*/.local-operator
           PYTHONPATH=<worktree>  PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=<scratch>  CMUX_* stripped
tests/unit/evaluation/runner/test_compact_action_binding.py            14 passed in 4.84s
tests/unit/evaluation/test_session_arm.py -k "header or platform"      18 passed, 149 deselected in 7.21s
flake8 --max-line-length=100 <both touched files>                      exit 0
docstring-stripped AST equality, base vs head                          True / True
89 rendered prompt cases, sha256 base vs head                          identical
df before each run: 1.9-3.3 GiB free (never below the 1.5 GiB stop line)
```

**Not run:** the full unit suite (CI owns it; nothing here can affect it — no executable byte changed), pyright (absent from the shared venv), any VM or paid episode, and no re-audit of round-1-approved code. Worktree removed after the run; the shared `~/local-operator` checkout and its staged work were not touched.

### Verdict

`clean` — no BLOCKER, no MAJOR. **This round is TERMINAL.** n1–n3 are body/comment wording follow-ups, not a reason for another round.
